items.root_cause: a commodity's scope and its search term live in two files and nothing ties them: q-2026-09-18-4-laundry-scope widened the rule in commodities.json and reversed 10 known-wrong rulings, and the term that decides what every term-rotation store (and Baker's weekly-ad routing) actually asks stayed on the one brand the old rule was written for. No check asks whether a term reads as its own commodity.

root_fix.what: audit-search-terms.ps1 routes every commodity's first term through the engine matcher and lists each one that reads as no commodity (a listing, not a gate: 37 of 634 after this fix), and its -SelfTest freezes the founding term and the laundry case: every live laundry-detergent term must read as laundry-detergent and name no brand, three brands' liquids must land in the cell, and pods, sheets and powder must not. grocery/README.md's term guidance, which held 'arm and hammer detergent' up as the good broad example, now says a brand term asks for one brand and that a widening carries its term.
root_fix.exact_change: Get-TermScope and Get-EngineCommodityId; a SEARCHTERMS-SCOPE listing and 'scope none N of M' on the SEARCH-TERMS-COMPLETE marker; 14 new self-test cases and a literal case count (23)

items.leaves_open: five liquid laundry detergents the widened rule still cannot read, none cheaper than the crown: Arm & Hammer Baking Soda Fresh liquids (Walmart 110 fl oz 0.0815, Baker's 0.0894 and 0.0999) are refused by the global \bsoda\b and sparkling excludes, and at Aldi Gain Original Detergent 132 FL OZ (0.1208) and Tide Simply Detergent 31 fl oz (0.1110) carry neither laundry nor liquid in the name. 5 products over 3 stores in the seeded captures. Widening the rule is a scope question, not a term fix, so it is filed as Q-laundry-rule-gaps.

blast_radius.measured_by: the term: live read-only answers at Family Fare (Freshop) and Baker's (Kroger API) at the production limit of 25, routed through the engine; the exclude: before/after routing of 772 laundry-shaped names over 572 files (plan-2026-09-25-3.routing.json) and apply-coverage-batch in a scratch clone
blast_radius.risk: A search term moves no row by itself: rows reach the board only when a store capture asks the term. The term was measured at Family Fare and Baker's live (read-only) and over the seeded captures; the four browser stores (Walmart, Sam's Club, Aldi, Fareway) cannot be probed headless, so the first capture there is the measurement. Walmart's in-store lane is store-scoped, but a broad term can surface a bulk seller shape (FOCA 287.42 fl oz is already in the soundness baseline), which rules/grocery.md warns is a seller shape, not a brand. Predicted from the probe, not yet on the board: Family Fare's laundry cell would move from Arm & Hammer Odor Blasters 138 fl oz 0.1014 to Our Family Free & Clear 50 fl oz 0.0838, a newly found cheaper real product; Baker's best new-term liquid is Arm & Hammer Sensitive Skin 170 fl oz 0.0823 against its 0.0804 cell. Nothing found beats the Aldi crown 0.0549, so the crown does not move on this evidence.

open_questions_for_brad.question: The widened laundry-detergent rule still cannot read five liquid products in the seeded captures: Arm & Hammer Baking Soda Fresh liquids at Walmart and Baker's (blocked by the board-wide soda and sparkling excludes, which exist for drinks), and at Aldi Gain Original Detergent 132 FL OZ and Tide Simply Detergent, whose names say neither laundry nor liquid. None is cheaper than the Aldi crown (the cheapest is Walmart's 0.0815, equal to its current cell). Should the rule admit them?
options: A: admit them: release the soda and sparkling excludes for laundry-detergent, and admit a detergent name with a fl oz size and no dish or dishwasher word, through apply-coverage-batch
B: leave them: the crown is unaffected and each store's cell is already priced from another liquid
open_questions_for_brad.recommendation: A, through the matching lane with its gates: the rule is any liquid laundry detergent, and a product the rule means but cannot read is how a cheaper one would be missed later
